cohort: The study included 180 participants (90 in each group) with term pregnancies undergoing either elective or emergency cesarean sections.
finding: Emergency cesarean sections were associated with significantly higher postpartum haemorrhage, maternal ICU admissions, lower APGAR scores, increased NICU admissions, and higher rates of neonatal septicemia compared to elective cesarean sections.
mod_finding: Emergency cesarean sections resulted in more adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes compared to elective cesarean sections.
